question: Can a policy trained only on public Veritas maintenance observations learn action selection and verification while beating or matching explicit public-belief and inspect-verify-retry controls on fresh worlds?
parent: DEV-049A reliability and DEV-050A public Veritas verification, both development results

environment.task_generator: unchanged DEV-050 final amended public generator, not canonical/sealed Veritas

teacher: inspect_verify_retry (only public observations; oracle labels never given to training code)
admissibility: Only isolate if slot free and not already isolated; service only if isolated with attempt count <2; DONE and INSPECT are always selectable, so safety is not encoded into admissibility

models.architecture: small MLP (12 public belief features -> 32 -> 4 actions) without privileged future/hidden state

calibration.selection: choose minimum physical cost gated policy on disjoint calibration worlds subject to zero observed residual faults and blocked actions, otherwise use teacher-only fallback; no evaluation-dependent selection
calibration.selection_scope: per model seed; once before final eval

evaluation.primary: residual faulty entities and complete-world fraction under native runtime independent verifier
evaluation.safety_guard: Learned policy is not declared superior if any residual faults exceed reference, even if cheaper

integrity: freeze source and protocol before fitting
checkpoint SHA256 and raw per-world outcomes per policy, per seed
train labels constructed only from public records and observed action callback receipts
independent replay of frozen models and real Veritas native transitions
include every failed/blocked action and tool expense
strict split identity and no DEV050 world reuse
limitations: Known two-entity and opaque-ID task; no new dynamics/partial sensing/domain shift
Hand-coded belief teacher and heuristic safety fallback remain baseline and may outperform models
Student-state aggregation uses extra simulator interactions; matched updates not equal FLOPs
This is not complete TAC-OSM learned recurrent memory nor cross-domain transfer
Zero observed failures cannot certify real-world safety
No threshold or model tuning on sealed evaluation
